newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soymeal export deals total 200,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Indian soymeal export deals total 200,000 tonnes.

text.p: India has so far signed export deals for 200,000 tonnes of soymeal for November-December shipments, traders said on Tuesday.

"Around 100,000 tonnes of soymeal have been contracted between $245-250 per tonne (FAS) 45 days ago and another 100,000 tonnes in the range of $265-275 per tonne for November-December shipments in the last fortnight," said a leading oilmeal trader.
Davish jain, chairman of the Soybean Processors Associaiton of India (SOPA) said on Friday that exporters had signed contracts for nearly 150,000 tonnes of soymeal exports.
Satyanarayan Saboo, another leading oilmeal trader, said export demand was mainly from China, Indonesia, South Korea and some Gulf countries.
Traders said the main buyers were Hong Kong-based Concordia Agri Trading, Cargill Hong Kong Ltd, Singapore's Peter Chemer, Continental Grains, G. Premjee Ltd and Germany's Alfred Toeffer.
The companies could not be reached for comment.
Soymeal prices on Tuesday were quoted at $275-276 per tonne FAS (free alongside ship) compared to about $204-205 per tonne at the same time last year.
Traders last week said importers were booking orders on fears that lower soymeal availability from India during 1996/97 (Nov-Oct) might further push up prices.

Small quantities from the fresh soybean crop had started arriving in some markets of Western India. But harvesting was still to begin in Central India, which accounts for nearly 80 percent of the country's total soybean output, traders said.
Trading for the new soybean crop started at 13,250 rupees per tonne and was currently quoted at 13,100 rupees.
Export orders for the 1995/96 crop were booked at $285 per tonne, sharply up from $185-188 per tonne at the start of the season in November, traders said.
Spot soybean was quoted at 13,050-13,250 rupees per tonne in plant delivery condition, traders said.
